traditional.label: Traditional Council
traditional.source: ACDT DRR SOP Development_Traditional Council Questionnaire(1).docx
traditional.purpose: Purpose: Gather the Traditional Council’s input into the four practical SOPs that will implement the existing approved DRR and Resilience Implementation Plan.
traditional.opening: Opening statement for the facilitator: “The DRR Plan is already in place. Today’s discussion will help us develop simple procedures explaining when action is needed, who does what, who must be contacted and what must be recorded. We would like to understand current arrangements and your recommendations for improving them.”
traditional.approach: Facilitation approach: Ask the main questions in plain language. Use the prompts where needed, and request examples from actual incidents. Distinguish current practice from proposed arrangements and identify matters requiring confirmation or authorisation.

questions.question: What responsibilities should the Traditional Council have in implementing the DRR Plan?
questions.prompts: What does the Council already do? Which responsibilities need clarification?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: Who should be the Council’s main contact for DRR matters?
questions.prompts: Who is the alternative when that person is unavailable? How should their contact details be shared and kept current?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: Which actions can the Council take directly, and which require authorisation or referral?
questions.prompts: Who makes decisions within the Council? Which matters must go to ACDT, Monte View, municipal disaster management or emergency services?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: How should the Council coordinate with DRR Wardens and other institutions?
questions.prompts: Who reports to whom? Which communication channels should be used? What happens when there is no response?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: How should DRR decisions and outstanding actions be recorded and followed up?
questions.prompts: Who keeps the record? Who receives reports? How should revised procedures be communicated?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: When a risk identified in the DRR Plan is observed or reported, what should the Council do?
questions.prompts: Who receives and checks the report? Who arranges preventive action? When must the matter be referred?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: What should the Council help check before a high-risk season or anticipated event?
questions.prompts: Contact persons, volunteers, venues, transport and other resources. Who follows up on gaps?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: How should an early warning be checked and communicated to residents?
questions.prompts: What is the trusted source? Who confirms the message? Who communicates it? How are rumours corrected and people without phones reached?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: How should evacuation arrangements be prepared in advance?
questions.prompts: Suitable routes and assembly points; permission to use venues; transport; arrangements for notifying residents. Who must verify their suitability?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: How should residents who may need additional assistance be identified and supported?
questions.prompts: Older persons, children, persons with disabilities and people with limited mobility. Who maintains necessary information, protects it and updates arrangements?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: When the Council receives an emergency report, what should happen first?
questions.prompts: What details are needed? Who checks the report? Who must be contacted immediately?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: What should trigger the mobilisation of the Council’s support?
questions.prompts: Who initiates it? Who acts if the designated person is unavailable? Which situations require immediate contact with emergency services?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: How should the Council organise its support during an emergency?
questions.prompts: Who coordinates Council activities? Who liaises with Wardens, responders and ACDT/Monte View? Who communicates verified information to residents?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: What should the Council do when residents need to move to safety?
questions.prompts: How are authorised instructions relayed? Who helps mobilise transport and venues? How is assistance arranged for vulnerable residents?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: How should community resources and volunteers be mobilised safely?
questions.prompts: Who requests and authorises their use? What tasks are suitable? Which tasks must be left to trained responders?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: What should happen when responders arrive and when immediate danger has passed?
questions.prompts: Who provides information and hands over coordination? Who communicates that it is safe to return or stand down? What must be recorded?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: How should the Council help establish who has been affected and what assistance is needed?
questions.prompts: Who gathers and verifies information? How are urgent and unmet needs referred? How do we avoid excluding households or duplicating records?
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

questions.question: What role should the Council play in requesting and supporting relief distribution?
questions.prompts: Who submits requests? How are needs prioritised fairly? Who records assistance received and distributed?
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

questions.question: How should residents raise complaints or report that they have not received necessary assistance?
questions.prompts: Who receives concerns? Who refers them? How are residents informed of the outcome?
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

questions.question: How should the Council contribute to recovery that reduces future risk?
questions.prompts: Restoring services and livelihoods; safer repair or rebuilding; identifying priorities; referring matters requiring technical advice or approval.
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

questions.question: How should the Council review an incident and follow up on improvements?
questions.prompts: Who participates? What worked or failed? Who is assigned corrective actions? How is completion confirmed?
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

traditional.scenario_instruction: Brief scenario check: For each situation below, ask: “What should the Council do first, whom should it contact, and what specific community support would be needed?”

scenarios.question: Flooding and severe weather
scenarios.prompts: Warning, access, evacuation and temporary shelter arrangements.

scenarios.question: Fire and electrical incidents
scenarios.prompts: Immediate notification, keeping residents away from danger and support for displaced households.

scenarios.question: Water interruption, drought and extreme heat
scenarios.prompts: Reporting, communicating verified information and supporting people most at risk.

scenarios.question: Medical and public-health incidents
scenarios.prompts: Contacting relevant health services, communicating authorised advice and protecting privacy.

scenarios.question: Community-safety incidents
scenarios.prompts: Contacting the appropriate authorities, safe communication and avoiding actions that escalate tensions.

scenarios.question: Mining-related and environmental incidents
scenarios.prompts: Reporting to relevant institutions, communicating verified instructions and keeping residents away from hazardous areas.

closing: What are the three most important arrangements that these SOPs must make clear?
Which proposed responsibilities or arrangements need confirmation by other institutions?
What support would the Council need to carry out its agreed role?

wardens.label: Wardens and General Stakeholders
wardens.source: ACDT DRR SOP Development_DRR Wardens Questionnaire(1).docx
wardens.purpose: Purpose: Gather the trained DRR Wardens’ practical input into the four SOPs that will implement the existing approved DRR and Resilience Implementation Plan, drawing on their previous training, local knowledge and experience.
wardens.opening: Opening statement for the facilitator: “We previously worked together on DRR training, and the DRR Plan is already in place. Today’s discussion will help us turn that foundation into simple procedures you can follow in practice. We want to understand which arrangements are clear, where difficulties remain, and what steps, contacts and tools you need to carry out your responsibilities safely.”
wardens.approach: Facilitation approach: Build on the Wardens’ previous training without assuming that every procedure is already understood or operational. Ask the main questions in plain language and use the prompts where needed. Request examples from incidents, training exercises or local observations. Distinguish current practice from proposed arrangements, and identify matters requiring confirmation or authorisation.

questions.question: Based on your training, what are your responsibilities as DRR Wardens, and which need clarification?
questions.prompts: What have you been able to put into practice? Which tasks are outside your role, training or authority?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: How should Warden responsibilities be organised across the community?
questions.prompts: Who covers each area? Who coordinates the Wardens? Who acts when a Warden or coordinator is unavailable?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: Who should you report to, and which actions require authorisation or referral?
questions.prompts: What can you do immediately within your role? Who authorises other actions? When must you contact emergency services directly?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: How should you communicate with other Wardens, the Traditional Council, ACDT, Monte View and relevant services?
questions.prompts: Which channels work reliably? Who maintains contact details? What happens when a contact does not respond?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: How should routine observations, decisions and outstanding actions be recorded and followed up?
questions.prompts: Who completes and receives records? Who checks progress? How should changes to procedures be communicated to all Wardens?
questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison

questions.question: When you observe or receive a report of a risk identified in the DRR Plan, what steps should you follow?
questions.prompts: What information should you check and record? Who receives the report? What safe preventive action can you take, and what must be referred?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: What should you check regularly and before a high-risk season or anticipated event?
questions.prompts: Warden availability, contacts, communication devices, equipment, transport and other resources. How should gaps be reported and followed up?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: How should you receive, verify and communicate an early warning?
questions.prompts: Which sources are trusted? Who confirms or approves the message? How do you reach people without phones and confirm that warnings were received?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: What should you do in advance to prepare for an evacuation?
questions.prompts: Routes, assembly points, access, transport and assigned responsibilities. Who confirms suitability? How should arrangements be practised and updated?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: How should you prepare to assist residents who may need additional support?
questions.prompts: Who may need help receiving warnings or moving to safety? How is assistance arranged? What information is necessary, who may access it, and how is it kept current?
questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning

questions.question: When you receive an emergency report or discover an incident, what should you do first?
questions.prompts: What details are needed? How do you assess immediate danger safely? Which urgent notifications or actions must not wait for further verification?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: What should trigger the activation of the Wardens, and how should this happen?
questions.prompts: Who initiates activation? How are available Wardens contacted? What happens outside normal hours or when the coordinator is unavailable?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: How should Wardens organise themselves at an incident?
questions.prompts: Who coordinates community support until responders arrive? How are tasks allocated? How do you maintain communication and avoid conflicting instructions?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: How should you support residents moving to safety?
questions.prompts: Who gives evacuation instructions? How do you guide people, assist vulnerable residents and account for arrivals or missing persons? How are missing persons reported without undertaking unsafe searches?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: How should you recognise when a task is unsafe or beyond your training and authority?
questions.prompts: What should you avoid? When should you withdraw, keep others away and request specialist assistance? What if equipment is unavailable or communication fails?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: What should you do when responders arrive and when the incident is stood down?
questions.prompts: What information and records should you hand over? Who confirms stand-down or safe return? How do you account for Wardens and equipment and report unresolved needs?
questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response

questions.question: How should you gather and report information about affected households, urgent needs and damage?
questions.prompts: What minimum information is needed? How is it verified safely? Which assessments require specialists? How are duplicate records avoided and urgent needs escalated?
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

questions.question: What steps should you follow when supporting relief requests, receipt and distribution?
questions.prompts: Who authorises assistance? How are supplies and recipients recorded? How are needs prioritised fairly and shortages or discrepancies reported?
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

questions.question: How should you handle unmet needs, complaints or concerns about assistance?
questions.prompts: Who receives referrals? How are concerns recorded confidentially? Who follows up and informs the affected person of the outcome?
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

questions.question: How should you support recovery that reduces future risk?
questions.prompts: What continuing risks should you report? How can you track restoration of services and livelihoods? Which repair or rebuilding decisions require technical advice or approval?
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

questions.question: How should you contribute to closing an incident and improving future readiness?
questions.prompts: What records must be completed? What worked or failed? Who follows up corrective actions? What equipment, procedure or refresher-training needs should be recorded?
questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better

wardens.scenario_instruction: Brief scenario check: For each situation below, ask: “Drawing on your training, what would you do first, whom would you contact, what would you avoid, and what would you record?”

scenarios.question: Flooding and severe weather
scenarios.prompts: Warning dissemination, safe routes, evacuation support, assembly-point accountability and escalation; avoiding floodwater and unsafe rescue attempts.

scenarios.question: Fire and electrical incidents
scenarios.prompts: Immediate notification, keeping people away from danger, evacuation support and reporting; limits on firefighting and contact with electrical equipment.

scenarios.question: Water interruption, drought and extreme heat
scenarios.prompts: Reporting conditions, communicating verified advice, checking on vulnerable residents and referring urgent needs.

scenarios.question: Medical and public-health incidents
scenarios.prompts: Contacting health services, assistance within training, following authorised advice and protecting personal information.

scenarios.question: Community-safety incidents
scenarios.prompts: Safe observation and reporting, contacting appropriate authorities and avoiding confrontation or unauthorised intervention.

scenarios.question: Mining-related and environmental incidents
scenarios.prompts: Reporting location and observable conditions from a safe position, communicating authorised instructions and avoiding hazardous areas or substances.

closing: What are the three most important things these SOPs must make clear for Wardens?
Which arrangements require confirmation by the Traditional Council, ACDT, Monte View or external services?
What additional tools, equipment or refresher training would help you apply the SOPs safely and consistently?

district.label: District Municipality
district.source: Armoede municipal consultation questionnaire developed for local officials and district disaster management centres
district.purpose: Gather district municipality officials’ input on risks, services and coordination affecting Armoede / Ga-Sekhaolelo, to inform the four community SOPs.
district.opening: Answer from your institution’s actual role in Armoede. Describe current arrangements and local examples, then identify proposed improvements and matters needing confirmation. This consultation does not approve procedures or commit resources.
district.approach: Use the main questions and follow-up prompts to record your institution’s responsibilities and its interface with the other sphere of government and community structures. Keep answers specific to Armoede. Leave questions outside your role unanswered or identify the responsible institution. Distinguish existing arrangements, proposals and matters requiring confirmation.

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: What district disaster management functions and support arrangements cover Armoede?
questions.prompts: Describe the district centre’s area of coverage, coordination, technical advice and support to the local municipality. Which services are provided directly, which rest with local government or other institutions, and what responsibilities need clarification?

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: How should Armoede and the local municipality reach the district disaster management centre?
questions.prompts: Identify official duty functions, operating hours, after-hours alternatives and emergency reporting routes. Which community reports may go directly to the district, and which use the local channel? How are receipt, incident references and escalation confirmed?

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: How should the district centre coordinate Armoede matters with the local municipality and community structures?
questions.prompts: Who is the district liaison? How do the Traditional Council, ACDT, Monte View and wardens participate through agreed channels? How can village stakeholder teams link to municipal and district coordination forums? Explain feedback to Armoede.

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: Which district decisions or approvals may be needed during an incident affecting Armoede?
questions.prompts: Clarify authority for district resource support, coordination arrangements and referrals to provincial or specialist services. Which decisions remain with local or other competent authorities? How are requests and delegations documented without assigning statutory authority to volunteers?

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: How should district planning and capacity support incorporate Armoede’s risks and community SOPs?
questions.prompts: Describe the status of district and local disaster management plans, relief arrangements and support to local policy development. What technical, training or staffing support can be considered for Armoede? Separate available support from proposed commitments.

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: What district risk information or technical assessments could help prioritise Armoede’s hazards?
questions.prompts: What maps, incident records and assessments cover the community? Which evidence needs verification with local officials and residents? Consider storm, flood, fire, water, public-health and mining or environmental risks and potential effects beyond local boundaries.

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: How can the district support preventive action and seasonal preparedness in Armoede?
questions.prompts: How are local maintenance or service risks referred to the responsible institution? Describe technical advice, readiness reviews and coordination with service providers. How are unresolved Armoede risks escalated and progress communicated back?

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: How should the district centre receive, verify and relay warnings relevant to Armoede?
questions.prompts: Identify authorised warning sources, duty monitoring and the local municipal contact. How are affected areas, impact, protective action and update times communicated? How does the district obtain feedback on local dissemination, correct misinformation and support communication failures?

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: What district support is needed to verify evacuation and shelter arrangements for Armoede?
questions.prompts: Who supports hazard screening, route and venue suitability, capacity, accessibility and coordination of transport or neighbouring facilities? How are findings agreed with the local municipality and community structures? Explain joint exercises and updates.

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: How should district services support inclusive preparedness for Armoede residents needing assistance?
questions.prompts: How does the district coordinate with local government, health, social services and transport providers? What referral arrangements support people who may miss warnings or struggle to move safely? Describe secure information-sharing without entering personal household details.

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: How should the district centre handle an incident notification concerning Armoede?
questions.prompts: What information is required from the local municipality or community, who logs and assesses it, and how is the appropriate lead service notified? Explain prompt acknowledgement, immediate life-safety escalation and requests for missing information without delaying urgent response.

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: What should trigger district mobilisation or escalation beyond the district for an Armoede incident?
questions.prompts: Describe indicators of exceeded local capacity, specialist needs or wider impacts. Who authorises support, requests provincial or mutual assistance and updates the local municipality? Identify after-hours procedures and constraints without promising unconfirmed response times.

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: How should the district coordinate multiple agencies supporting an incident in Armoede?
questions.prompts: How are the local lead, district coordination function and specialist responders linked? Who consolidates situation updates and resource requests? How is community information received and how do wardens and the Trust support the response safely?

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: How can the district support evacuation and shelter needs that exceed local capacity in Armoede?
questions.prompts: Who coordinates additional transport, receiving facilities, welfare, safeguarding and links to health or social services? Which competent authority issues protective instructions? How are people accounted for and information shared with local officials?

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: How should the district arrange specialist resources and service-provider support for Armoede?
questions.prompts: Consider rescue, fire, medical services, electricity, emergency water, environmental health, roads and mine-related technical advice. What request and mobilisation process applies, what mutual support exists and how are communication or access failures addressed?

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: How should the district support stand-down and the transition to recovery in Armoede?
questions.prompts: Which lead service confirms remaining hazards and safe-return advice? How are district resources accounted for and outstanding issues handed to local or sector recovery functions? How does consistent information reach the local municipality and residents?

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: How should district personnel support and consolidate damage and needs assessments for Armoede?
questions.prompts: Which common information and verification arrangements are used? When are technical teams needed and who requests them? How are local and community reports consolidated, duplication avoided, urgent needs escalated and personal information protected?

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: How should district relief coordination support affected Armoede residents?
questions.prompts: Describe how local requests reach responsible departments or relief partners, how eligibility and unmet needs are tracked and how overlapping assistance is avoided. What district records, allocation decisions and reconciliation are needed? Distinguish confirmed resources from requests.

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: How should the district help resolve unresolved relief or service concerns affecting Armoede?
questions.prompts: Which cases should first go to local government or a service provider, and which need district escalation? Who tracks referrals, follows up delayed responses and gives the community an outcome through accessible channels?

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: How can district recovery support reduce repeated losses in Armoede?
questions.prompts: What technical coordination, planning support or funding referrals can assist safer infrastructure repairs, service restoration and livelihoods? How do local priorities reach sector departments or provincial processes? Identify approval, ownership and maintenance responsibilities.

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: How should the district and local municipality review Armoede incidents and track learning?
questions.prompts: Who convenes joint reviews and includes community feedback? How are corrective actions, district support needs and outstanding risks followed up? What joint exercises or training would test the local and district interface?

district.scenario_instruction: For each Armoede scenario, describe the first notification, local lead, district support or escalation, safe community role and records needed. State what exists now and what still needs confirmation. These are discussion scenarios, not verified incident reports.

scenarios.question: A severe storm damages homes and blocks or floods access to Road One or New Stands in Armoede
scenarios.prompts: District response: explain support to the local municipality, coordination and escalation. How are warnings relayed, access and damage assessed, rescue or evacuation referred, and temporary shelter arranged? What changes if mobile communications fail or local responders are already deployed elsewhere?

scenarios.question: A veld or household fire threatens Armoede residents while damaged electrical infrastructure creates additional danger
scenarios.prompts: District response: explain support to the local municipality, coordination and escalation. Which fire service and electricity operator are notified? Who coordinates safe access, isolation, protective instructions and shelter? What can wardens safely support, and when is district assistance requested?

scenarios.question: Armoede experiences a prolonged water interruption during extreme heat
scenarios.prompts: District response: explain support to the local municipality, coordination and escalation. Who verifies the cause and restoration plan with the responsible water provider? How are safe emergency supply, vulnerable residents, water quality, public messages and distribution records addressed? What district support is needed?

scenarios.question: A suspected public-health incident or cluster of illness is reported in Armoede
scenarios.prompts: District response: explain support to the local municipality, coordination and escalation. How are health services and environmental health notified? Who verifies the concern, provides authorised advice and arranges necessary assistance while protecting privacy? Which municipal and district functions support the health lead?

scenarios.question: A community-safety incident disrupts access to emergency or essential services in Armoede
scenarios.prompts: District response: explain support to the local municipality, coordination and escalation. How do municipal and district contacts coordinate with the appropriate safety authorities and community liaison structures? How are safe access, verified public messages and continuity of essential support maintained without involving volunteers in enforcement?

scenarios.question: A suspected mining-related or environmental incident could affect Armoede’s water, air or access
scenarios.prompts: District response: explain support to the local municipality, coordination and escalation. Who receives the community report and refers it to the operator, responsible regulator, environmental health and disaster management contacts as appropriate? Who verifies impacts, obtains specialist advice and communicates protective action without asking wardens to enter hazardous areas?

closing: What are the three most important district support arrangements the Armoede SOPs must make clear?
Which arrangements can your institution confirm, and which require agreement from other authorities, service providers or Armoede community structures?
What priority support, training, equipment, assessment or planning action would improve district support for Armoede?

local.label: Local Municipality
local.source: Armoede municipal consultation questionnaire developed for local officials and district disaster management centres
local.purpose: Gather local municipality officials’ input on risks, services and coordination affecting Armoede / Ga-Sekhaolelo, to inform the four community SOPs.
local.opening: Answer from your institution’s actual role in Armoede. Describe current arrangements and local examples, then identify proposed improvements and matters needing confirmation. This consultation does not approve procedures or commit resources.
local.approach: Use the main questions and follow-up prompts to record your institution’s responsibilities and its interface with the other sphere of government and community structures. Keep answers specific to Armoede. Leave questions outside your role unanswered or identify the responsible institution. Distinguish existing arrangements, proposals and matters requiring confirmation.

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: Which local municipal functions and service providers are responsible for risks and services affecting Armoede?
questions.prompts: Identify the departments covering Armoede, their current duties and gaps needing clarification. Distinguish the municipality’s own functions from those of the district, water or electricity provider, health services and other authorities.

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: Who should Armoede contact at the local municipality for routine risks and urgent incidents?
questions.prompts: Describe the receiving function, duty arrangements outside office hours, alternative when unavailable, acknowledgement and incident reference. How does an unanswered request reach district disaster management or emergency services? Use official channels rather than private contact numbers.

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: How should the local municipality work with Armoede’s Traditional Council, ACDT, Monte View and wardens?
questions.prompts: Who maintains community liaison and convenes discussions? How do community reports enter municipal work planning? How should village stakeholder teams link to existing ward and municipal structures? Describe how the community receives feedback.

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: Which decisions affecting Armoede can local officials take, and which require district or specialist approval?
questions.prompts: Identify the decision-maker for municipal resources, protective instructions, shelter use and requests for specialist support. Which delegations are confirmed? Clarify community support roles without assigning statutory powers to the Trust or wardens.

questions.section: SOP 1: Governance, Institutional Coordination and Interagency Liaison
questions.question: How should Armoede’s needs be reflected in local disaster management and municipal service planning?
questions.prompts: What plans and relief policies are approved, being developed or awaiting approval? How are Armoede priorities linked to municipal planning, budgets and maintenance work? Discuss current staffing, training needs, action tracking and feedback.

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: What risk assessments or site inspections are needed in Armoede?
questions.prompts: Which hotspots and past incidents should guide inspections? Consider Road One, New Stands, storm damage, drainage, fire, electrical hazards, water interruptions and environmental concerns where relevant. Who participates, records findings and requests district technical support?

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: What preventive maintenance and seasonal checks should the local municipality arrange for Armoede?
questions.prompts: Consider drainage, culverts, roads, waste, water and other assets under the responsible provider. Who owns each asset, receives work requests and checks completion? Identify what can be done locally and what needs another provider or district support.

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: How should the local municipality relay verified warnings and protective advice to Armoede?
questions.prompts: How are warnings received from district centres or authorised sources, translated into locally relevant messages and shared through community contacts? Describe correction of rumours, alternative channels during outages and checks that residents received the message.

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: How should local officials help verify routes, assembly places and shelters serving Armoede?
questions.prompts: Who checks safety, access, capacity, accessibility, water, sanitation and permission to use venues? Who arranges transport and alternative access? Explain the district or specialist input needed and how arrangements should be practised with the community.

questions.section: SOP 2: Risk Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness and Early Warning
questions.question: How should local services prepare assistance for Armoede residents who may need extra support?
questions.prompts: How are community structures linked to social, health, transport and other responsible services? Consider accessible warnings, mobility and continuity of care. Describe consent and secure referral arrangements without recording household names or health details here.

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: What should happen when Armoede reports an incident to the local municipality?
questions.prompts: What location, hazard, access and life-safety information is needed? Who logs, triages and refers the incident? How are emergency services notified without waiting for a completed form, and how does the community receive acknowledgement and updates?

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: When and how should local officials request district assistance for an Armoede incident?
questions.prompts: Identify triggers such as overwhelmed responders, blocked access, multiple affected households or specialist needs. Who makes and receives the request, what information is required and what happens after hours? State existing arrangements and matters needing agreement.

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: How should local municipal responders coordinate with Armoede community structures at an incident?
questions.prompts: Who is the lead service for the hazard? Who receives local information, assigns safe support tasks and liaises with the district? How are conflicting instructions avoided and community records handed over to responders?

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: How should the local municipality support authorised evacuation and temporary shelter for Armoede?
questions.prompts: Who confirms instructions, assesses access, requests transport and manages receiving venues? How are people needing assistance, missing-person referrals and shelter accountability handled? Which needs must be escalated to the district or another institution?

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: How should local officials arrange specialist help and essential services for Armoede when resources are constrained?
questions.prompts: Consider fire, rescue, medical response, electricity isolation, water, environmental health and access. Identify the responsible provider, district support route and communication fallback. What tasks can volunteers safely support, and what requires trained responders?

questions.section: SOP 3: Emergency Activation, Incident Coordination and Priority Hazard Response
questions.question: How should local officials communicate stand-down, safe return and recovery handover to Armoede?
questions.prompts: Which competent authority checks remaining hazards and authorises the decision? Who informs community structures and the district? What records, outstanding needs and resource accounts pass to recovery teams?

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: How should the local municipality assess damage and urgent needs in Armoede?
questions.prompts: Who verifies community reports and arranges technical infrastructure or environmental assessments? How are urgent needs referred, duplicate records avoided and district assistance requested? Describe minimum necessary information and privacy controls.

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: How should local officials coordinate relief requests and distribution support for Armoede?
questions.prompts: Who receives requests, determines eligibility or refers them to the responsible department? How are shelter, water, food and other needs prioritised? Explain district referrals, ACDT support, receipt and distribution records and tracking of unmet needs without assuming funding is approved.

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: How can Armoede residents follow up delayed municipal services or relief?
questions.prompts: Describe accessible service-request and complaint channels, case references, escalation and feedback. How are excluded households referred for review? Distinguish routine complaints from emergencies requiring immediate notification.

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: What local recovery and maintenance improvements would reduce repeat disaster losses in Armoede?
questions.prompts: Consider drainage, roads, water services, safer repairs, community facilities and affected livelihoods. Who owns the work, provides technical approval, requests funding and maintains the restored assets? Which priorities need district or other institutional support?

questions.section: SOP 4: Relief, Recovery and Build Back Better
questions.question: How should local officials and Armoede stakeholders review incidents and confirm corrective actions?
questions.prompts: Who convenes reviews with wardens, the Trust, the Traditional Council and responders? How are actions tracked and reported to the district where needed? What exercises, equipment checks and training should test local readiness?

local.scenario_instruction: For each Armoede scenario, describe the first notification, local lead, district support or escalation, safe community role and records needed. State what exists now and what still needs confirmation. These are discussion scenarios, not verified incident reports.

scenarios.question: A severe storm damages homes and blocks or floods access to Road One or New Stands in Armoede
scenarios.prompts: Local response: explain local notification, responsible services, community liaison and district support requests. How are warnings relayed, access and damage assessed, rescue or evacuation referred, and temporary shelter arranged? What changes if mobile communications fail or local responders are already deployed elsewhere?

scenarios.question: A veld or household fire threatens Armoede residents while damaged electrical infrastructure creates additional danger
scenarios.prompts: Local response: explain local notification, responsible services, community liaison and district support requests. Which fire service and electricity operator are notified? Who coordinates safe access, isolation, protective instructions and shelter? What can wardens safely support, and when is district assistance requested?

scenarios.question: Armoede experiences a prolonged water interruption during extreme heat
scenarios.prompts: Local response: explain local notification, responsible services, community liaison and district support requests. Who verifies the cause and restoration plan with the responsible water provider? How are safe emergency supply, vulnerable residents, water quality, public messages and distribution records addressed? What district support is needed?

scenarios.question: A suspected public-health incident or cluster of illness is reported in Armoede
scenarios.prompts: Local response: explain local notification, responsible services, community liaison and district support requests. How are health services and environmental health notified? Who verifies the concern, provides authorised advice and arranges necessary assistance while protecting privacy? Which municipal and district functions support the health lead?

scenarios.question: A community-safety incident disrupts access to emergency or essential services in Armoede
scenarios.prompts: Local response: explain local notification, responsible services, community liaison and district support requests. How do municipal and district contacts coordinate with the appropriate safety authorities and community liaison structures? How are safe access, verified public messages and continuity of essential support maintained without involving volunteers in enforcement?

scenarios.question: A suspected mining-related or environmental incident could affect Armoede’s water, air or access
scenarios.prompts: Local response: explain local notification, responsible services, community liaison and district support requests. Who receives the community report and refers it to the operator, responsible regulator, environmental health and disaster management contacts as appropriate? Who verifies impacts, obtains specialist advice and communicates protective action without asking wardens to enter hazardous areas?

closing: What are the three most important local municipal arrangements the Armoede SOPs must make clear?
Which arrangements can your institution confirm, and which require agreement from other authorities, service providers or Armoede community structures?
What priority support, training, equipment, assessment or planning action would improve local services and response in Armoede?
